display_name: Pedro Ernesto Alonso De Los Reyes

wanted_details.heading: Court-record details
wanted_details.status: Charged by indictment announced January 23, 2025; not sentenced as of the Justice Department's May 6, 2026 release

details.label: Arrested
details.value: In the Netherlands on January 10, 2025, on a United States warrant

details.label: Co-defendants
details.value: Jin Sung-Il, Pak Jin-Song, Erick Ntekereze Prince, Emanuel Ashtor

details.label: Charges
details.value: Conspiracy to cause damage to a protected computer, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and mail fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and conspiracy to transfer false identification documents

wanted_details.caution: According to the indictment, over the course of their scheme, from approximately April 2018 through August 2024, the defendants and their unindicted co-conspirators obtained work from at least sixty-four U.S. companies. Payments from ten of those companies generated at least $866,255 in revenue, most of which the defendants then laundered through a Chinese bank account. As part of this prosecution, the FBI arrested Ntekereze and Ashtor and executed a search of Ashtor’s residence in North Carolina, where he previously operated a “laptop farm” that hosted victim company-provided laptops to deceive companies into thinking they had hired U.S.-located workers. Alonso was arrested in the Netherlands on Jan. 10, pursuant to an arrest warrant from the United States. According to the indictment, the defendants used forged and stolen identity documents, including U.S. passports containing the stolen personally identifiable information of a U.S. person, to conceal the true identities of Jin, Pak, and other North Korean co-conspirators, so that these North Korean nationals could circumvent sanctions and other laws to obtain employment with U.S. companies. Ntekereze and Ashtor received laptops from U.S. company employers at their residences, downloading and installing remote access software on them, without authorization, to facilitate IT worker access and to perpetuate the deception of U.S. companies.
wanted_details.remarks: The Justice Department's May 6, 2026 release states: Ashtor is awaiting trial, de los Reyes is in custody in The Netherlands awaiting extradition, and the Sung-il and Jin-Song are fugitives.

disclaimer: Pedro Ernesto Alonso De Los Reyes is a Mexican national, not a DPRK national, and is profiled here as a facilitator charged in the January 2025 indictment alongside Jin Sung-Il and Pak Jin-Song. He was arrested in the Netherlands on January 10, 2025 on a United States warrant, and the Department's May 2026 release says he remains in custody there awaiting extradition. Jin Sung-Il's FBI notice lists Pedro Alonso and Pedro Alonso de los Reyes among the aliases Jin used, and that overlap is recorded on Jin's profile, not resolved here.

The confidence level of 'confirmed' reflects that this individual is named in a federal indictment described in Justice Department releases; the conduct is alleged, and every person named is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law.
